messages.text:
"Mobile landscape top-down firefighter rescue game called Mr. Rescue: Extinguish Protocol. Pixel art style inspired by classic Mr. Rescue (red helmet firefighter, yellow suit, burning multi-room buildings with furniture and windows). The game must fill the entire phone screen in landscape mode with no black bars.

Full mobile controls (required): Dual virtual joysticks that appear on touch. Left side of the screen = movement joystick. Right side of the screen = aim and continuous fire joystick. Always-visible bottom button to cycle/switch between Water, Foam, Cryo, and CO2. Show current extinguisher type clearly. All controls must work fully with touch only.

Extinguisher system: Instead of fast-depleting ammo, each extinguisher has a short spray burst followed by a 10-15 second cooldown before it can be used again. Correct extinguisher must visibly affect its matching enemies (clear death/extinguish effect with particles and color change). Wrong extinguisher has little or no effect and shows feedback.

Four distinct fire enemy types with unique looks and colors so they are easy to identify:
- Water targets: bright orange/yellow flames
- Foam targets: darker oily/smoky or magma-like
- Cryo targets: pale blue/white frostfire
- CO2 targets: purple or green gas ghosts

Core loop: Rescue civilians (pick up/carry or escort to exits/windows). Heat rises near fire. Fire spreads. Score based on rescues and efficiency. Multiple rooms per floor; clear by rescuing most civilians then reach the exit. Successfully escorting a civilian to the exit must clearly update the score and rescue count.

High-impact features:
- Synergy extinguishers: Correct type on enemies can create combo effects (Water + Cryo freezes nearby, Foam + CO2 creates sticky cloud). Wrong type does nothing or backfires.
- Heat as risk/reward: High heat strengthens your current extinguisher but increases fire spread and makes civilians panic/run randomly. Low heat is safer but weaker.
- Civilian variety: Some run to exits alone, some freeze in fear, some follow you, some grab items. Interact to change their behavior.
- Room objectives with twists: Rescue X civilians before a timer, protect a civilian while extinguishing a specific type, or clear one enemy type first.
- Temporary power-ups: Aim assist, extinguisher overcharge (area damage), coolant suit (slower heat but slower movement), etc.
- Living fire system: Fires have states (smoldering → active → raging). Some grow if ignored, others calm if enemies are cleared. Vents spread fire between rooms.
- Style scoring: Combos for efficient extinguishing, undamaged rescues, and fast room clears. End-of-floor grade (S/A/B/C).
- Light rogue-lite progression: Permanent small upgrades between runs (extra starting ammo or shorter cooldown, slower heat, new civilian types, enemy variants).

Enemy patrols that block rescues: Circular guards around trapped civilians, doorway blockers, line-of-sight sweepers, figure-8 cross patrols, expanding leash guards, and enemies that chase you once you pick up a civilian. Trapped civilians are often protected by these patterns, requiring timing, correct extinguisher, or clearing the guard first.

Challenging and tense. UI shows heat bar, current extinguisher + cooldown, score, civilians remaining, and style grade. End of floor requires most civilians rescued. Everything must be fully playable with mobile touch controls only. Hide any debug overlays.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
